text:
Jordan Kyrou spent his whole career in St. Louis before landing in Washington, and he's been one of the Capitals' most efficient scorers. He has 14 points in 15 games while playing only 14:34 a night, which works out to 3.85 points per 60, and seven of those points came on the power play.

Some of that is hot hands. Five goals on 2.2 expected (the quality of his chances) means he's shooting 21%, double last season's 10%. But his teammates have scored 4.2 fewer goals than their chances with him on, so the assists have room to grow while the goals slow. The surprising part of his profile is defense: Evolving-Hockey had him 99th percentile among forwards at taking chances away last season, and most of his value came there, not from scoring. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds that he carries the puck in more than half the time and gets to the slot. If Tom Wilson misses time after Saturday's ejection, a winger this productive in limited minutes is an obvious candidate for more ice. Watch the minutes.
headline: Kyrou is doing a lot with a little
